points.description: States abstraction as a main advantage of object-oriented programming (hiding implementation detail and exposing only essential features), using the term 'abstraction'.
points.partial_credit: Half marks if the idea of hiding details/showing only essentials is described precisely but the term 'abstraction' is not used.

points.description: States reusability as a main advantage of object-oriented programming (code/classes can be reused, e.g. via inheritance), using the term 'reusability' or 'reuse'.
points.partial_credit: Half marks if reuse of existing code/classes (e.g. via inheritance) is described precisely but the term 'reusability/reuse' is not used.

rubric.notes: Both advantages, abstraction and reusability, are required; each is worth half the marks and must be named precisely. Vague benefits (e.g. 'easier to code', 'organised', 'real-world modelling') earn nothing. A wrong claim about either point, or naming only one, loses the other point's marks as stated; a wrong extra advantage does not earn marks but a wrong statement about abstraction or reusability voids that point.
